picks.headline: In Praise of the Translators Who Transport Us Across the Globe
picks.excerpt: An argument for literary translation as cultural infrastructure and skilled craft, set against survey data showing translators losing work and income to generative AI. A craft-side counterweight to the industry's rush toward AI-assisted book translation.
picks.rationale: Net-new URL, distinct from every published books card. A craft counterweight that reframes literary translation as skilled human labor against the AI-translation push - the strongest creative/craft hook in the pool.

picks.headline: Researchers to Investigate Local Editor and Publisher AI Use
picks.excerpt: University of Melbourne and RMIT researchers are surveying editors and publishers about how they actually use generative AI tools in independent publishing practice. A grounded look at where AI is entering real editorial and production workflows, rather than the hype.
picks.rationale: Net-new URL and a distinct outlet (Books+Publishing). Actionable and workflow-grounded - maps where generative AI genuinely enters editorial and production practice rather than the litigation/hype cycle. Distinct accent since it shares the books category.

picks.headline: Poetry Foundation Library Scraped, Used to Make AI-Generated Educational Content
picks.excerpt: Giggle Academy, a 'free learning' platform founded by Binance's CZ Zhao, scraped hundreds of copyrighted poems from the Poetry Foundation to auto-generate illustrated lessons and storybooks with no human curation. A concrete look at AI-generated creative/educational content at scale - and what fully-automated book-making does to poets and publishers.
picks.rationale: Kept as a recovery pick for its genuine creative-production hook - fully-automated AI book-making (illustrated storybooks and lessons) at scale, not merely the copyright angle. Distinct event from the published Google/Gemini and UDel Google Books scraping cards; net-new URL and a third distinct outlet (Publishers Weekly).
